meta.title: 仕組み · yokoten
meta.description: Follow your agent through one task: its own sandbox keeps rm -rf away from the project next door, the guard stops a force push, and the checks run before and after the push.

intro.label: 仕組み
intro.title: ひとつのタスクを順番に
intro.body: 「再生」を押すか、「次へ」で一歩ずつ進めます。

player.label: いまのステップ
player.ready: 準備できました。「再生」を押すか、「次へ」で一歩ずつ進めます。
player.red: 止められた、失敗した、またはあなた待ち
player.green: 許可された、または通った

steps: You run npx yokoten in your project. It turns on your agent's own sandbox.
You give your agent a task.
The agent edits a file in the project. The sandbox lets it through.
The agent runs rm -rf on the folder next door. The sandbox refuses: it can't write there.
The agent tries a force push. The guard stops it.
The agent commits. The commit check looks for secrets and personal data.
The pull request goes to GitHub. CI runs the same check again.
リリースとタグはあなただけです。

questions.label: 質問
questions.title: サンドボックスについて

items.q: My agent already has a sandbox. What does yokoten add?
items.a: Most agents ship with it off, or with a way around it. yokoten turns it on for the project. For Claude Code it also closes the way around: if the sandbox can't start, commands don't run.

items.q: What does the sandbox not protect?
items.a: The folder the agent starts in. Start it in one project, not in your home folder.

Claude Code and Codex: yokoten turns one on in the project's settings. Grok: yokoten writes a sandbox profile, and you start Grok with --sandbox yokoten. Gemini CLI, Muse and the others have no project sandbox, so they get the guard only.
